correctness.rationale: On all complex matrices the Hilbert–Schmidt orthonormal Weyl basis is W_(a,b)/sqrt(N). The columns for Tr(PH) are the distinct characters of the shift–modulation group times A(a,b)/sqrt(N) up to phase; the character norm N gives singular values sqrt(N)|A(a,b)|, including zeros. Expanding e_3(x+a)+e_3(x) gives off-diagonal quadratic coefficients t+a_i+a_j, t=|a| mod 2. When t=0 the polar image has dimension two except when a is zero or all ones; the latter case is even-weight only for even n. For t=1 the kernel condition is x=s(1+a)+u1 with s=1·x and u=a·x: consistency forces s=u for odd n, and leaves two independent parameters for even n. Thus the ranks for odd shifts are n-1 and n-2, respectively. Squaring the Walsh transform leaves a radical character sum: its squared modulus is either zero or N times the radical size, so Parseval gives exactly 2^r coefficients of modulus 2^(n-r/2). Counting the N/2 odd shifts and the two types of even shifts gives the three stated multiplicities, including the even exceptional all-ones shift. The levels are distinct for n>=5. Their extrema give the stated positive-subspace condition number and the rank densities follow by division by N^2. This does not assert nonlinear phase-retrieval injectivity. The frozen checker and numeric verification notes were inspected, not rerun; the all-size argument does not depend on them.

evidence: Write c_b=|<psi,P_(a,b)psi>| for one odd a and r=n-(3+(-1)^n)/2. Eq. (106) gives sum c_b^4=2^(-r), Eq. (107) gives sum c_b=2^(r/2), and Walsh Parseval gives sum c_b^2=1 since the translation derivative is a sign function.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Hölder gives (sum c_b^2)^3 <= (sum c_b)^2(sum c_b^4), and the stated sums attain equality. Equality makes every positive c_b identical, so there are exactly 2^r such entries of size 2^(-r/2). Half the shifts are odd; multiplying the per-shift count by N/2 and using the even table gives all multiplicities. Standard Weyl scaling and reading off the extreme levels yield the entire claimed spectrum, rank and condition number with no new classification needed.

evidence: The product of all controlled-Z triple phases gives precisely psi(x)=2^(-n/2)(-1)^e_3(x). A normalized Pauli coefficient has magnitude |A(a,b)|/N; changing from ZX to the Hermitian Pauli convention contributes only a unit phase. Appendix F.1 conditions on the same translation a (called x there) and varies modulation b (called z there).
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: A signed zero-frequency autocorrelation or a derivative count alone would not be enough; the prior appendix covers all modulations per translation in the required magnitude convention. The lifting singular values are N^(3/2) times these normalized Pauli magnitudes, with the same multiplicities.

originality.rationale: Chen–Yan–Zhou already analyze the identical complete three-uniform state's normalized Pauli coefficients by translation parity, not only its global moments. Their Appendix F.1 Eqs. (108)–(110) give the even-shift magnitudes and counts directly. Their Eqs. (106)–(107) give a fourth moment and a first absolute moment for each odd shift. Together with unit per-shift Parseval these saturate Hölder, forcing the precise odd-shift nonzero magnitude and multiplicity. Consequently the whole ambiguity histogram is mechanically recoverable from the prior appendix. The usual Weyl-to-lifting diagonalization rescales it; the compact polar-rank proof is another derivation, not a distinct claimed spectrum.
residual_risks: This review establishes exact implication, not priority for the first literal statement in Gabor singular-value notation. The published journal text timed out, but the decisive lawful arXiv version was read directly.
